# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — teach the prompt that solutions are graded on multiple same-layout files → write general, data-driven code
- Changes I made (prompt.md only; tools.py is NOT in the editable artifact set this iteration):
  - Step 2 (NEW knowledge): code is re-run on SEVERAL spreadsheets sharing the layout but with different data/size → detect extents at runtime; never hardcode a row count / range size / matched value / position from the sample. (Cluster: overfit-to-sample — 418-29, 374-9, 160-6, 53161, 52216.)
  - Step 3 (NEW/clarify): answer_position is the WRITE target, not the read extent — read input dynamically; Cell-Level = write exactly the listed cells; Sheet-Level = real row/col deletion that shifts remaining data (delete_rows), not a local clear. (Cluster: read-only-answer-range + wrong delete semantics — 418-29, 374-9, 160-6, 347-49.)
  - Step 1 (rewrite+WHY): inspect real cell coordinates before computing (preview hides layout); use data_only=True to read formula cells; blank may be None or "". (Cluster: layout misread — 53161, 347-49.)
  - Step 4 (kept + added WHY): kept "prefer literal values" and added that the grader recalculates formulas on open; deliberately did NOT forbid formulas.
  - Step 5 (NEW): preserve untouched sheets/cells; prefer in-place openpyxl over DataFrame rebuild.
- Expected effect + safety: raises the 5 flaky + several always-fail tasks by making the good behavior (dynamic, correctly-placed writes) consistent. Safe because both passing tasks already satisfy every new rule — 47484 (dynamic pandas, literals) and 40467 (in-place openpyxl, correct formula to fixed D1:D10); no rule forces a different action or graded output for them, and none loosens a decision/permission.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first iteration (LEDGER baseline-only, ./prior_iterations empty).
- Refuted hypotheses (proven THIS iteration, do not re-test): "never write formulas / always literals" is WRONG as a hard rule — 40467 scores 1.0 on all 5 trials writing an Excel formula, so the grader recalculates formulas; a forbid-formulas edit would regress it. The formula/literal axis is NOT the failure cause (only 52216 t0 ever wrote a formula); the real cause is overfitting to the single visible sample.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 55457 (blank instruction — intent unknowable, no safe general edit) and 32468 (task-specific 12-month rolling SUMIFS logic). Deep per-task logic errors that a general prompt cannot target without overfitting.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this prompt-only edit under-delivers, the next lever is tool-code enforcement (a compute/validation helper in tools.py) — but that requires tools.py to be added to the editable artifact set.
- Focus next iteration: measure whether the generalization rule moved 418-29/374-9/160-6/53161 to consistent 3/3; if flakiness persists, consider a few-shot `<example>` showing dynamic detection (find last row, search markers) as an explicit template for the reader.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.527 Δ=+0.087 · fixed={160-6, 418-29, 53161} · broke={40467}.
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.527 Δ=+0.087 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — kill the wasted round-1 (tool-call-XML) + exact literal-format matching
- Changes I made (prompt.md only; tools.py not in editable set):
  - NEW "OUTPUT CONTRACT" block at the very top: reply with EXACTLY ONE ```python fence, NEVER tool-call XML (`<function_calls>`, `<invoke name="execute_python">`, `<invoke name="computer">`, `<parameter name="code">`); only fenced code runs; a non-fenced reply wastes one of ~5 rounds. (Cluster 1: wasted-round-on-wrong-format.)
  - NEW sub-bullet under step 4: reproduce a literal result format the instruction shows character-for-character; pick the format code that yields it (`01`→`dd`, `05`→`00`, `Jan`→`mmm`); `1-Jan` where `01-Jan` was shown is graded wrong. (Cluster 2: literal-format-precision.)
- Expected effect + safety:
  - Contract: measured 23/50 trials this iteration emit tool-call XML on round 1 and burn a round (harness "No python code block was found"), concentrated in the failing/flaky tasks (32468 5/5, 52216 5/5, 55457 5/5, 347-49 3/5, 40467 3/5, 374-9 2/5). All 4 passing tasks waste 0/5 → they already fence, so the rule changes none of their actions; it only returns a usable round to the tasks that fumble it. Safe & additive.
  - Format: 40467 t0 (0.0) used `d-mmm`→`1-Jan`; its 4 passing siblings used `dd-mmm`→`01-Jan` (instruction literally shows `01-Jan`). Rule fires only when a literal format is shown and "match it exactly" is the graded-correct behavior, so no passing task can be flipped. Recovers 40467 (seed 1.00 → cand_0001 0.80).
- Building on prior RESULTS: kept ALL of cand_0001's accepted generalization rules (steps 1–5) unchanged (it was ACCEPTED, fixed 160-6/418-29/53161). Did NOT re-try forbidding formulas — cand_0001 refuted it (40467 passes 3/3 writing a formula).
- Refuted hypotheses (do not re-test): "never write formulas" (cand_0001). Also: prose alone cannot fix the deep-logic 0.00 tasks (32468/55457) — confirmed again; their answers are per-task and hidden test files 2&3 are unavailable.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 32468 (rolling-12-mo SUMIFS), 52216 (which cell drives the INDEX-MATCH region lookup — seed got 2/5 so it IS solvable; the winning trial read region from `INPUTS!A14` and wrote literals), 347-49 (delete blank rows above each "Gross Pay" marker), 374-9 (output-row mapping fails identically on hidden files 2&3 → always [1,0,0], a real generalization gap I can't pin without the files). 55457 unknowable (blank instruction).
- Plateau signal: n/a (2nd iteration, cand_0001 was +0.087). If this prompt-only lever plateaus, the next lever must be tools.py (a compute/validation helper or a code-executor that rejects non-fenced replies) — but that requires tools.py to enter the editable artifact set.
- Focus next iteration: check whether removing the wasted round moved the 5/5-wasted tasks (32468, 52216, 55457) and whether 40467 returned to 1.00; if 374-9 stays [1,0,0], its output-row mapping is the next target (needs the hidden-file layout, or a rule tying output rows to the destination sheet's own labels rather than the source rows).

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.547 Δ=+0.020 · fixed={40467} · broke={—}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
